entries.spec-flow/specs/spec_graph_791-retire-of: 11 — was 8; #797 adds 2 and #795 adds 1. #797 retired the SUBJECTS of two #791 demands (the live projection stage, and spec_graph_774.yaml itself), so both became waivers, and a waiver's rationale owes a `cites` to a claim in its own graph's ledger. #791 has no claim about a change that had not happened yet, and inventing one would be a fabricated probe. The rules those demands carried are re-asserted live in defender/tests/test_797_retirement.py. #795's +1 is `three_evals_skip_loudly`, which now dangles: its subjects were the three retired-stage eval entry points this graph made skip-but-keep-running (secondary_eval, judge_equivalence, run_judge_ab); two have since been retired outright and the third went with them, so the test that witnessed the loud skip was deleted with its subjects. In both cases the graph is a record of what shipped and is not being rewritten to un-ship it; the demands are moot rather than unmet. The other 8 are unchanged and still the first to clear.

Clearing c12 — re-running that census and recording what it sampled — returns this graph to clean and the entry is trimmed on the next --update-baseline, and c12's own `note:` records that census already being re-run once (counts corrected by G13), so that is the cheaper way out of this entry than it reads.
